findings.title: Concurrent anonymous uploads can still stall the builder and wall — the changed full-length transcoder starts an unrestricted ffmpeg process per request for up to 900 seconds
findings.observed: Concurrent POSTs launch uncapped ffmpeg jobs with a 900-second timeout.

findings.title: Oversized anonymous uploads can still exhaust disk and interrupt other crews — multipart files are spooled before the changed upload handler checks their size
findings.observed: FastAPI parses the multipart body before video.read(MAX_UPLOAD + 1) enforces 60 MB.

findings.title: A former holder of the reviewer's verified email can keep reviewing private clips briefly after losing it — the admin guard caches a positive allowlist decision for five minutes
findings.observed: A cached positive email check grants admin for up to 300 seconds after email removal.

findings.title: The reviewer cannot take an accidentally approved clip off the public wall — the changed rejection route accepts approved clips but the admin page never lists them
findings.observed: The review page lists only pending clips, so an approved clip has no Reject control.

findings.title: Crews can post a long video without choosing its length — the upload API defaults missing or invalid keep values to full and never measures duration
findings.observed: A >60s POST without keep is accepted and stored in full instead of returning 4xx.

findings.title: Crews can upload long footage without a warning or length choice — metadata errors, nonfinite duration or an eight-second timeout are treated as a short video
findings.observed: Unknown video duration triggers send(f, "full") without a warning.

findings.title: Visitors see no Clip of the Week when approved clips have no likes — the selector rejects every zero-like clip
findings.observed: Approved clips with 0 weekly likes produce clip_of_week=null and no banner.

findings.title: Visitors can see an old clip crowned Clip of the Week instead of this week's winner — the selector never filters clips by posting date
findings.observed: A month-old clip with more recent likes wins over all clips posted this week.

findings.title: Crews can submit the same long clip multiple times or cancel after it is already uploading — the three warning actions remain enabled throughout send
findings.observed: Pressing a warning action again during upload starts another POST or resets the warning.

findings.title: Visitors cannot tell when the featured clip is broken — the new banner video has no error handler or fallback
findings.observed: A failed featured video remains a blank player without the clip error message.

findings.title: A failed clip post still leaves private footage stranded in cloud storage — the changed upload stores the object before the Mongo insert without rollback
findings.observed: A failed clips.insert_one leaves the uploaded MP4 object behind.

findings.title: Crews can still submit duplicate clips after a lost response — the changed upload creates a new ID on every retry without an idempotency key
findings.observed: Retrying an accepted upload after a lost response creates another pending clip.

findings.title: Crews still lose approved wall posts and the true weekly winner as the wall grows — the changed list ranks only 500 unsorted rows and returns 60 without pagination
findings.observed: An approved clip outside the first 500 can never enter the wall or featured ranking.

findings.title: Visitors still see stale standings and an outdated Clip of the Week after liking — the changed optimistic update never reranks or refreshes the banner
findings.observed: Liking a runner-up leaves the old banner; a first like leaves the banner absent.

findings.title: Rejected crew videos can still be played from caches for a day — the changed serving helper retains public 24-hour caching for wall clips
findings.observed: Public video responses remain cacheable for 86400 seconds after rejection.

findings.title: Clients still cannot change roles through the specified admin endpoint — the changed role handler is registered at /api/users instead of /api/admin/users
findings.observed: PATCH /api/admin/users/{id}/role has no route.

findings.title: Wall API consumers still cannot read a clip's crew_name — the changed listing returns only the stored crew key
findings.observed: GET /api/clips returns crew but omits crew_name.

findings.title: Crews cannot link an older device-built kit to a shoot video — the new kit history discards all but the latest ten
findings.observed: Building an 11th distinct kit removes the oldest kit from the upload selector.

findings.title: Crews can accidentally submit an earlier video after choosing a replacement — the file button stays enabled while the asynchronous duration check is running
findings.observed: Choosing a second video during metadata loading can send both videos.

findings.title: The owner can see old non-allowlisted admins and demote the only real reviewer without the promised 409 — old roles are corrected only when each user next signs in
findings.observed: A previous admin stays stored as admin until they sign in; the last-admin count includes them.

findings.title: The reviewer can be locked out of the queue after a transient identity-provider failure — the new mandatory allowlist lookup has no handled failure path
findings.observed: A Clerk user lookup error propagates from /api/me and admin routes as a server error.

findings.title: Crews can still unknowingly post under the wrong name — the changed shoot uploader and server accept an empty crew and substitute Phnom Penh crew
findings.observed: An empty or whitespace-only crew posts as "Phnom Penh crew".

findings.title: Phone viewers can still wait for the whole clip before playback or seeking — the changed response helper downloads the entire storage object before serving ranges
findings.observed: A first byte-range request fetches the entire stored MP4 before slicing.

findings.title: Visitors still are not told when a like was not saved — the changed banner and grid handler catches the error and silently reloads
findings.observed: A failed POST /clips/{id}/like silently reloads without a failure message.

findings.title: Wall visitors lose most of a landscape shoot when playing it — the featured player and grid force every video into a portrait object-cover frame
findings.observed: A landscape shoot is played inside a 9:16 object-cover frame, cropping its sides.

findings.title: Visitors can see the wrong Clip of the Week once more than 5,000 clips receive weekly likes — the new ranking uses a capped, unsorted like aggregation
findings.observed: Weekly like groups after the first 5000 are omitted and their clips rank with 0 likes.

findings.title: Crews cannot attach a kit that appeared to build successfully when its database save failed — the new selector remembers every returned ID even if the create endpoint swallowed the write error
findings.observed: An unsaved kit is selectable, but posting with its ID returns 404 "Kit not found".

findings.title: Crews cannot tell which length they chose while their video uploads — the warning never records or marks the selected mode
findings.observed: While posting, both length choices remain visually identical and neither is marked selected.

findings.title: Wall visitors still cannot tell when a crew's clip was posted — the changed tile does not render its posted time
findings.observed: Wall cards still omit the returned created_at.

findings.title: The reviewer is offered a role change that can never work — the user-management dropdown still lists admin after the server forbids all admin promotions
findings.observed: Selecting admin for any listed member always shows "Couldn't change the role".

findings.title: Khmer-speaking visitors lose their selected language when opening a wall clip's kit — the new full-page link remounts the app with the default English state
findings.observed: Opening a wall kit in Khmer reloads the app with lang="en".
